instruction.text: This is the second scene of the film. Read the scene and answer the questions.

atoms.text:
Act I, Scene II

(Captain Joth is pressing buttons at the spaceship’s controls with multiple of their many arms.)

Captain Joth: We are right on track and should be landing very soon.

Doctor Loyt: (pleased) Great news! And we haven’t even encountered any turbulence! I hate turbulence.

Captain Joth: (shocked) You didn’t just … (trailing off and then, angrily shouting) YOU JUST JINXED IT! Never say out loud that we’ve had no turbulence. Now we’ll encounter turbulence for sure!

Doctor Loyt: (laughing) Nonsense! I’m a scientist, I don’t believe in so-called jinxing. There is no such thing.

(The spaceship suddenly rocks and shudders. A calculator flies off the table and towards Captain Joth’s head. Kozzer yelps and runs for Doctor Loyt, who catches it.)

Doctor Loyt: (paling) Oh no!

Captain Joth: (angrily) What did I tell you? (running over to the screens) The brakes are failing. This will make for a very (screaming the words) TURBULENT CRASH LANDING! I hope you’re happy! (strapping themselves tightly into their seat) Hold on tight!

(Doctor Loyt hurries to the seats and holds on tightly to Kozzer. Kozzer tries to soothe Doctor Loyt. Lights flash and alarms blare. The ship continues to rock and shudder. After a few minutes, the ship crashes and everything goes black.)

Select the adjective that matches Captain Joth’s belief.

hint.text:
To be superstitious means to believe that certain actions can bring bad luck.
The word superficial means on the surface of something.

instruction.text: What happened first? Put the events of the scene into the correct order.

atoms.b: Captain Joth announces the spaceship is due to land soon.
Doctor Loyt jinxes their easy flight and the brakes fail.
Both Doctor Loyt and Captain Joth strap into their seats with Kozzer soothing Doctor Loyt.
